vulnerabilities.title: 'PHP2Shell' Critical PHP Flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) - NCSC Patch-or-Isolate Alert Forces UK Councils, NHS Boards and Met Police Sites Offline
affected_products: PHP (unpatched supported branches; check php.net advisory for exact versions)
vulnerabilities.summary: UK government and public sector. Press reports (STV News, Insurance Business, Lancashire Evening Post) say the NCSC, with EU and Australian counterparts, urged immediate patching of two critical PHP flaws nicknamed 'PHP2Shell' (CVE-2026-109618/109619, both reported at CVSS 9.2) that can allow unauthenticated remote takeover of a web server. NCSC advice: patch at once; if not possible apply PHP's temporary mitigations; if that is also not quick, consider taking affected systems offline. In response, at least seven of Scotland's 32 councils and six NHS health boards pulled public websites, and Edinburgh and Oxford councils, South Ribble Borough Council, the Met Police and Golden Jubilee Hospital were reported affected. Most sites were restored within hours to the next morning after patching. No confirmed in-the-wild exploitation was found in the sources; the takedowns were precautionary. NHS England Digital also lists PHP advisories dated 20-21 Oct. Details are from secondary reporting; NCSC primary text and PHP advisory were not retrieved. UPDATE 23 Oct: multiple security vendors now report in-the-wild exploitation - watchTowr (honeypot sightings), Patchstack (multiple confirmed incidents), Aikido and Cloudflare (early attack attempts); the Dutch NCSC says it is receiving partner signals of active weaponisation, while CISA had not observed exploitation as of its 21 Oct alert and the CVEs were not seen in KEV. Datadog states the widely circulated config workaround does not protect; only patching fixes it. No UK-specific compromise confirmed. UPDATE 24 Oct: fixed releases reported as PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 (PHP 8.1 and older unsupported; use vendor backports). Wiz, Tanium, Bitsight and Canada's Cyber Centre (AL26-026) have published guidance; KEV listing still not confirmed. UPDATE 25 Oct: SecurityWeek reports Mirai botnet operators joining PHP2Shell attacks and ASLR-bypass exploits emerging; Amazon threat intelligence reports first attempts from 17 Oct, ahead of the fix; joint NSA/CISA guidance urges immediate patching or taking unpatchable systems offline. Vendor accounts conflict on exploit reliability. KEV listing not confirmed. UPDATE 26 Oct: no new UK-specific compromise reported; NCSC guidance unchanged (patch to fixed releases or take unpatchable systems offline). KEV listing not confirmed. UPDATE 27 Oct: CISA added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to the KEV catalog on 26 Oct (alert 'CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog'), formally confirming in-the-wild exploitation (earlier 23 Oct CISA text said none observed). KEV due date not retrieved. VulnCheck reports an ASLR-aware x86-64 exploit against CVE-2026-109618 (customers only). No new UK-specific compromise confirmed; NCSC guidance unchanged. UPDATE 28 Oct: no new UK-specific compromise reported; NCSC CTO weekly summary (w/e 25 Oct) still urges immediate PHP mitigation. UPDATE 29 Oct: search summaries cite a Lords statement (Baroness Lloyd) that 32 central government services were unavailable and four partly affected, mostly precautionary, with no confirmed compromise of central government or wider public sector systems; some early compromise claims withdrawn. Amazon and honeypot reports of wider exploitation (incl. 35 live shells) remain unconfirmed by UK officials. UPDATE 30 Oct: no new UK-specific compromise reported; press (Irish News) cites a minister saying there was no breach of Budget security after the PHP flaw; NCSC guidance unchanged.
recommended_actions: Upgrade to PHP 8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35 or a vendor-backported fix; replace unsupported 8.1 and older.
Inventory all PHP-based web servers (CMS, intranets, legacy portals, third-party hosted council/NHS sites) and patch to the fixed PHP releases from php.net immediately.
Do not rely on the circulated config-only workaround (reported ineffective); prioritise patching.
Where patching is delayed, apply PHP's published temporary mitigations and restrict exposure via WAF/reverse proxy; isolate if neither is possible.
Hunt for webshells and unexpected child processes from PHP handlers; review web logs for anomalous requests since 2026-10-20.
Confirm suppliers and hosting providers have patched before restoring sites.

kql.name: Web server PHP process spawning shell
kql.description: Possible PHP2Shell post-exploitation: PHP/Apache/nginx parents spawning shells or download tools. Untested; tune.
kql.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php","php-fpm","php-cgi","php-fpm8","apache2","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","curl","wget","nc")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

kql.name: New PHP files written in web roots
kql.description: Hunts newly created .php files in common web directories (possible webshells).
kql.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName endswith ".php"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/var/www","/usr/share/nginx","\\inetpub\\wwwroot","htdocs")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine

iocs.context: Press coverage of PHP2Shell listed no IPs/domains/hashes; hunt on behaviour.

vulnerabilities.title: Legal Aid Agency (MoJ) Breach Scope Widened - Records Back to 1978 and HMPPS Probation Data Found in Stolen Set
vulnerabilities.vendor: UK Ministry of Justice / Legal Aid Agency
affected_products: Legal Aid Agency online services (2025 intrusion)
vulnerabilities.summary: UK central government. Per an agency update dated 2026-10-14 reported by CyberSecurityNews and GBHackers, forensic review of the 2025 Legal Aid Agency (Ministry of Justice) breach found the exfiltrated data goes further back than first disclosed: about 250,000 records pre-date 2007 and the earliest verified record is from 1978. Investigators also found probation data from HM Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) in the stolen material. The agency states it has no indication the data has been published or shared. This is a scope update to an older incident rather than a new intrusion, but it materially raises the sensitivity (applicants, defendants, probation subjects) and is the most significant UK government item found in the window. Details come from secondary reporting; the primary agency/MoJ notice could not be fetched.
recommended_actions: Organisations that supply or share data with MoJ/LAA should check for notifications and prepare for phishing and fraud aimed at affected individuals.
Monitor leak sites and dark-web markets for LAA/HMPPS-related data.
Review third-party and legacy-data retention: purge or archive-isolate pre-2007 records where legally possible.
Brief helpdesks on social-engineering using legal-aid or probation context.

kql.name: Phishing themed on Legal Aid / probation data breach
kql.description: Hunts inbound mail using breach-themed lures. Tune keywords.
kql.query:
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Subject has_any ("Legal Aid Agency","legal aid","HMPPS","probation","data breach notification")
| where SenderFromDomain !endswith "justice.gov.uk" and SenderFromDomain !endswith "gov.uk"
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, UrlCount, AttachmentCount

iocs.value: No technical indicators published for this scope update.
Data exfiltration of legacy case records; follow-on fraud/phishing against affected individuals
iocs.context: Expected downstream abuse of stolen legal-aid and probation data.

vulnerabilities.summary: UK police and public sector. A gblock article dated 28 Oct, citing The Record (27 Oct), reports that HMICFRS found hackers have repeatedly compromised third-party suppliers holding British police data since 2021, and that most supplier contracts carried no ongoing cybersecurity assurance. Context: earlier supplier breaches exposed officer data (e.g. ID-card supplier incidents affecting Met and Greater Manchester Police). Primary HMICFRS/Record text was not retrieved; details are secondary and unverified. Supply-chain exposure for forces and other public bodies using similar suppliers.
recommended_actions: Inventory suppliers holding police/public-sector personnel data and require ongoing security assurance in contracts
Review supplier access and data-sharing; monitor for phishing targeting officers/staff
Check NCSC supply chain security guidance

vulnerabilities.title: Carry-over: 'FortiBleed' - Stolen Fortinet Firewall Credentials Include UK Government, Embassy, Council and NHS Accounts Offered for Sale
affected_products: Fortinet FortiGate appliances (reported ~70,000-86,000 devices / credential sets, 194 countries)
vulnerabilities.summary: No new development found in the 2026-10-15 window (carry-over). Telegraph-led reporting from July 2026 says Russian-speaking actors harvested credentials from tens of thousands of Fortinet firewalls ('FortiBleed'); leaked/for-sale lists reportedly include IT staff at UK embassies (Thailand, Mauritius), local-authority staff (Derbyshire, Waltham Forest), and NHS, energy and medicine-supplier logins, with access priced up to ~$60,000. Counts vary by source (SOCRadar: 86,644 credentials). No formal state attribution and no NCSC/Fortinet PSIRT/CISA confirmation was found. This is NOT new in the 24h window - no fresh development was found - and is carried only because it is the most UK-government-specific credential exposure identified. Confidence is low; treat as a lead for credential rotation and exposure review.
recommended_actions: Rotate all credentials and secrets on FortiGate devices and any accounts authenticating through them; invalidate VPN sessions.
Patch FortiOS to the latest release and review for unknown admin accounts, config changes and exposed management interfaces.
Check dark-web/credential-leak monitoring for your domains.

kql.name: Fortinet - new admin accounts or config changes
kql.description: Detects admin/user creation and configuration changes in FortiGate CEF logs.
kql.query:
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where Activity has_any ("Add admin","Add user","Edit admin","Configuration changed","Attribute configured") or AdditionalExtensions has "cfgpath"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SourceIP, SourceUserName, Activity, Message
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

iocs.context: Per press reporting; no formal attribution.

iocs.value: No technical indicators identified for FortiBleed in this run.

vulnerabilities.title: Council Schools IT Network Hit by Second Cyber Attack - Records Exported (Bristol)
vulnerabilities.summary: Bristol24/7 reports a primary school served by a council schools IT network suffered a second cyber attack, with records exported in a data breach. Suspicious activity was spotted on 21 September when the first attack hit, but the network was not shut down until 25 September, which opposition councillors called 'very worrying'. The same actors are believed responsible for both attacks, though this is unconfirmed. Local-authority education is a recurring UK public-sector target. Single-source, secondary summary; scope and actor unconfirmed.
recommended_actions: Local authorities and MATs: review containment timelines and isolate school networks faster on suspicious activity.
Reset credentials after a first incident and confirm persistence is removed before restoring service.
Report to ICO, DfE and NCSC as required; check backups for offline copies.

kql.name: Large outbound transfers to file-sharing/cloud storage from school servers
kql.description: Exfiltration hunt; tune hostnames and thresholds.
kql.query:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("mega.nz","mega.io","anonfiles","transfer.sh","file.io")
| summarize Hits=count(), Hosts=dcount(DeviceName) by RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Hits desc

iocs.value: Repeat intrusion with data exfiltration after delayed containment
iocs.context: Reported pattern for the schools network.

vulnerabilities.title: Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation - NCSC and NHS England Alerts; UK Follow-on SAML Flaw Pending (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772, CVE-2026-107406)
affected_products: Hybrid Secure Private Access deployments using NetScaler
vulnerabilities.summary: UPDATE 2026-10-15: No NCSC update newer than the September advisory was found in the window; the NCSC continues to urge prompt mitigation, says it is still assessing UK impact, and warned that exploitation attempts would rise once patches and technical details were public (which has now happened: public PoC and mass 'spray and pray' scanning reported 2026-10-14). Mandiant says exploitation began in early September and affected North America and Europe. Sophos warns patching alone does not evict an attacker already on an appliance. Prior detail: UPDATE 2026-10-14: Help Net Security reports NetScaler exploitation has escalated from stealthy zero-day targeting into widespread 'spray and pray' attacks, fuelled by a published root-cause analysis and a public proof-of-concept exploit; Citrix and CISA confirm active exploitation and note patching alone may not remove access from an already-compromised appliance. No UK-specific victims were identified in search. The UK NCSC has told UK organisations to mitigate Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws promptly after confirming reports of active exploitation of CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution, CVSS 9.5, affects default configurations) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow leading to code execution or DoS, CVSS 9.5, requires DTLS, which is on by default for VPN virtual servers). Citrix disclosed them on 2026-09-27 (bulletin CTX697096) and CISA added both to KEV the same day with a 2026-09-30 federal deadline, but researchers report webshell deployment since early September, i.e. exploitation preceded disclosure. NHS England's National CSOC issued alert CC-4858 (2026-09-28) rating further exploitation 'almost certain', and a follow-on alert CC-4865 (updated 2026-10-09) covers a separate critical SAML memory-overflow flaw, CVE-2026-107406, which NHS CSOC assesses as likely to be exploited but which is not reported exploited. NetScaler is common in UK central government, NHS trusts, councils and corporate remote-access estates; no UK-specific exposure count was found (global counts range from ~21,000 to ~50,000 exposed instances depending on scanner). Post-exploitation reporting describes web shells (WHIPSHOT), a Python tunneller (SLAPSHOT) and a custom remote-management implant (Platypus) with a replaced customsnmpd. Patching alone does not evict an implant: appliances exposed since early September should be treated as potentially compromised. NOTE: this item is a carry-over/escalation from late September rather than a first report inside the 24h window; it is included because it is the only confirmed, actively exploited issue with direct NCSC and NHS England UK advisories and a pending follow-on CVE. Indicator detail comes from secondary vendor blogs - verify against Citrix's IoC scanner and the NCSC page. Primary pages could not be fetched directly in this run.
recommended_actions: Treat public PoC availability as raising urgency: patch internet-facing NetScaler now, and rebuild/replace any appliance exposed since early September rather than only patching.
Upgrade to 14.1-73.37 / 13.1-64.23 or later and then apply the fix for CVE-2026-107406 as it lands; do not rely on mitigation alone.
Run Citrix's IoC checker and review appliances for the listed file paths, unexpected .deb files and replaced customsnmpd; treat hits as full compromise.
Rotate credentials and secrets stored on or reachable from the appliance, and invalidate VPN sessions.
Restrict management and gateway exposure; forward NetScaler logs to Sentinel.
Follow NCSC and NHS England Digital cyber alerts CC-4858/CC-4865 for updates.

kql.name: Citrix NetScaler - exploitation artefact file paths
kql.description: Applies if NetScaler/Linux telemetry or file-integrity logs reach MDE. Otherwise port to FIM or syslog.
kql.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(45d)
| where FolderPath has_any ("/vpn/scripts/linux/","/var/netscaler/logon/LogonPoint/custom/")
| where FileName in~ ("nsgclient18.deb","nsg64.deb",".ctxs.receiver") or FileName endswith ".deb"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc

kql.name: Citrix NetScaler - post-patch outbound connections from appliances
kql.description: Populate ns_ips. Flags appliance-originated outbound connections to non-allow-listed public destinations (implant C2 / tunnelling).
kql.query:
let ns_ips = dynamic(["<NETSCALER_SNIP_OR_NSIP>"]);
let allowed = dynamic(["<NTP/DNS/UPDATE_IPs>"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
| where SourceIP in (ns_ips)
| where DestinationIP !in (allowed) and not(ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP))
| summarize Connections=count(), Ports=make_set(DestinationPort,20), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by SourceIP, DestinationIP
| sort by Connections desc

kql.name: Citrix NetScaler - suspicious activity in appliance syslog
kql.description: Looks for shell/webshell keywords in NetScaler syslog. Field names vary by build; tune.
kql.query:
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
| where Computer has_any ("netscaler","ns") or ProcessName has "nsppe"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("WHIPSHOT","SLAPSHOT","customsnmpd",".ctxs.receiver","nsgclient18","/bin/sh -c")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

iocs.context: Hidden artefact in LogonPoint custom directory.
Custom remote-management implant delivered after exploitation; replaced customsnmpd.

iocs.value: Full IP/hash lists (58 attacker IPs, webshell SHA-256) exist in Citrix IoC checker v1.4 / vendor reports and were not transcribed.

vulnerabilities.title: Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server OS Command Injection (CVE-2026-110447) Added to CISA KEV - Nextcloud Deployments at Risk
vulnerabilities.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-110447, an unauthenticated OS command injection in the Collabora Online built-in CODE server bundled with Nextcloud, to KEV on 23 Oct with a federal due date of 26 Oct. Exploitation allows arbitrary command execution, so web shells should be sought on unpatched hosts. Nextcloud is widely used for document collaboration by UK councils, universities and NHS suppliers, but no UK-specific compromise was reported. Details from search snippets and third-party reports; CISA page not retrieved.
recommended_actions: Update richdocumentscode to 26.4.303 or later, or remove the built-in CODE server.
Inventory Nextcloud instances (including supplier-hosted) and restrict Collabora endpoints from the internet where possible.
Hunt for web shells and unexpected child processes from the web server or CODE server.

vulnerabilities.title: CISA KEV Adds Cisco ASA/FTD SSL VPN DoS (CVE-2026-76418) and GitLab CVSS 10 RCE (CVE-2026-97229) - Edge/DevOps Exposure Relevant to UK Public Sector
affected_products: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD (SSL VPN)
vulnerabilities.summary: Not UK-specific: no UK victim identified. Secondary reports (The Hacker News, Rescana) say CISA added two exploited flaws to KEV on 29 Oct: a Cisco ASA/FTD SSL VPN denial-of-service (CVE-2026-76418) with no vendor IoCs published, and a GitLab unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-97229, CVSS 10.0) via a crafted regex in CI/CD config, linked to a failed exploitation attempt disclosed by Alpine Linux. Federal due date 1 Nov. Both product families are common in UK government and corporate estates (VPN perimeter, source-code/CI platforms), so exposure is plausible. Dates conflict slightly between outlets and primary CISA/vendor pages were not retrieved. Context: UK window otherwise surfaced no new dated UK government incident; the NCSC PHP2Shell alert (rank 1) remains the main UK-relevant item.
recommended_actions: Patch GitLab and Cisco ASA/FTD to fixed releases per vendor advisories
Inventory internet-exposed GitLab instances and ASA/FTD SSL VPN endpoints
Review GitLab CI/CD configs and runner logs for anomalous regex-heavy or newly added pipeline definitions

vulnerabilities.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support Authentication Bypass Exploited as Zero-Day by Suspected China-Nexus Actor - Added to CISA KEV 16 Oct (CVE-2026-102764)
vulnerabilities.vendor: BeyondTrust (vendor attribution disputed in one KEV snippet - Fortinet)
affected_products: BeyondTrust Remote Support (formerly Bomgar) 26.2.3 and earlier
vulnerabilities.summary: New in window. CISA added CVE-2026-102764, a critical authentication bypass in BeyondTrust Remote Support (versions 26.2.3 and earlier), to the KEV catalog on 2026-10-16 with a 2026-10-19 federal due date. A KLM security brief cites Mandiant as saying a suspected China-nexus espionage group exploited it as a zero-day from late August. Remote-support tooling is widely used by UK public sector bodies, MSPs and corporates and gives privileged access to endpoints, so exposure is relevant to UK government supply chains. Caveats: one KEV catalog snippet lists the entry under Fortinet rather than BeyondTrust, and the CISA alert itself could not be retrieved; CVSS not confirmed. Verify against the CISA catalog and vendor advisory.
recommended_actions: Upgrade BeyondTrust Remote Support to the fixed release per the vendor advisory; for cloud tenants confirm vendor patching.
Restrict internet exposure of the appliance and review session/admin logs since late August for unauthorised access.
Check MSP and third-party suppliers for BeyondTrust use and ask for assurance.

vulnerabilities.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Chained Zero-Days (Auth Bypass + RCE + Root Privilege Escalation) Exploited by UTA0576 - Added to CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935)
affected_products: Ivanti Connect Secure before 25.1.3.0 (22.7R2.14 and earlier reported unaffected)
vulnerabilities.summary: Volexity reports an actor it tracks as UTA0576 chained three Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days from 2026-10-03: an authentication bypass and RCE (tracked together as CVE-2026-104935) giving code execution as the cgi-server user, then a privilege escalation to root. Ivanti acknowledges 'limited exploitation in the wild'; CISA added CVE-2026-104935 to KEV on 2026-10-13 (federal due date reported as 2026-10-16). Fixes reported in 25.1.3.0/25.1.3.1/22.8R2.5 for two flaws; the third fix is reportedly still pending and no workaround is listed. Ivanti Connect Secure is widely deployed in UK government, NHS and corporate remote access and has a history of NCSC alerts (2024, 2025); no UK-specific victim was identified, but UK edge-VPN exposure makes this a priority hunt. Details come from search summaries (Hacker News/Forkast) and are unverified against Ivanti/CISA primary pages.
recommended_actions: Patch Connect Secure to the fixed builds immediately and apply any interim guidance for the unpatched third flaw.
Run Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool (noting past bypasses) and compare against known-good; if compromise suspected factory reset/rebuild and rotate all credentials and certificates.
Review appliance logs for unauthenticated requests to the API/auth endpoints from 2026-10-03.
Follow NCSC guidance on Ivanti exploitation.

kql.name: Ivanti Connect Secure - new outbound or admin changes
kql.description: Surfaces Ivanti appliance syslog showing config/admin changes or unexpected outbound flows since 2026-10-03.
kql.query:
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DeviceVendor has "Ivanti" or DeviceProduct has "Connect Secure"
| where Activity has_any ("admin","configuration","integrity","upload") or Message has_any ("cgi-server","setuid")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SourceIP, Activity, Message
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

kql.name: Outbound connections from Ivanti appliance management range
kql.description: Hunt for appliance-sourced connections to rare external hosts (set IvantiIPs).
kql.query:
let IvantiIPs = dynamic([]); // populate with appliance IPs
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where LocalIP in (IvantiIPs)
| summarize Conns=count(), Ports=make_set(RemotePort) by RemoteIP
| where Conns < 5
| sort by Conns asc
